key_insight: Convert structured skeleton data into a differentiable visual representation so off-the-shelf multimodal LLMs can directly reason about human pose and motion without lossy compression or brittle tokenization.
problem_solved: MLLMs cannot natively consume structured, non-visual skeleton data; prior approaches either collapse motion into lossy vectors or discretize into tokens that fail across diverse skeleton formats and motions.
method: Differentiable rendering: map skeletons (joints, bones, motion) to continuous, learnable visual proxy images/heatmaps so gradients propagate back to skeleton parameters.
Alignment with MLLMs: train/finetune the multimodal LLM to interpret rendered skeleton visuals via language supervision (captions, QA, prompts), enabling rich reasoning and downstream tasks.
Format-agnostic normalization: apply topology-agnostic preprocessing and a learned renderer so the pipeline generalizes across heterogeneous skeleton schemas and motion lengths.
impact: Enables MLLMs to handle structured pose/motion data robustly, unlocking unified solutions for action recognition, motion QA, animation editing, and biomechanics without bespoke tokenizers or format-specific models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: skeleton input → differentiable renderer → rendered image → MLLM → language output
Before vs after comparison: lossy vector/token methods vs SkeletonLLM's rendered representation (accuracy/generalization chart)
Renderer detail inset: joint-to-pixel mapping, motion heatmaps, gradient flow arrows showing end-to-end differentiability
Example use-cases: short text outputs for action captioning, pose QA, and motion editing with illustrative skeleton frames
paper_title: Universal Skeleton Understanding via Differentiable Rendering and MLLMs
paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Peiming Li, Xinshun Wang, Yang Tang, Kai-Kuang Ma
